transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-10-21 16:00 PDT | Duration: 54m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Clara Nguyen (Redwood SE), Lydia Park (BlueWave Head of ML), Tom Briggs (BlueWave Infra Lead), Maya Chen (Procurement), Eric Soto (Product), Speaker 6 (BlueWave)
---
Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be incomplete): Quick workshop to lock down POC acceptance thresholds, reporting format, and benchmark signals. Agreed on go/no-go candidates (latency p95, token cost delta, accuracy pass rate on labelled prompt set). Action items assigned for runbook, workload traces, and cost sims.
Topics: success metrics, workload sizing, benchmark cadence, reporting template, on-prem network constraints, SOC2/audit questions, timeline for decision.
Action items (auto section): see action items above.

Transcript: 
[00:00] Samir Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you blocking out the time. This is Samir from Redwood, I'm joined by Clara. The goal for today is to land on acceptance thresholds for the POC and the reporting format—so the BlueWave team can sign off on go/no-go criteria.
[00:18] Lydia Park: Thanks Samir. We're hoping to be pretty concrete today — we have compliance and product folks who need very specific pass/fail thresholds.
[00:27] Clara Nguyen: Great. Quick note — we'll refer to the benchmark spreadsheet, I'll drop a link after; it has slots for p50/p95 latencies, token-cost, and qualitative accuracy checks.
[00:36] Tom Briggs: One thing up front — our infra will likely run this in a VPC-connected private deployment for the pilot, may be on our GCP project. We need network egress and peering details. Also, we are concerned about cold-starts for the larger models.
[00:50] Samir Patel: Noted. We support Redwood Dedicated and Private flows — and for the POC it's fine to simulate both hosted and private. We'll need your VPC CIDR and an IP allowlist for the test run.
[01:05] Eric Soto: I want to confirm the timeline: we're looking for results within three weeks of starting test runs, because the risk review is on the 2nd of November.
[01:13] Maya Chen: Procurement needs a rough cost estimate to justify the pilot budget, so Clara if you can give us an approximate monthly burn for the Dedicated vs hosted path that'd be helpful.
[01:24] Clara Nguyen: Sure. I'll produce a sensitivity table. Very approximate now—assume burst QPS of 80, sustained QPS 25, seq length averages of ~512 tokens, and we'll model three model sizes: 7B quantized, 13B int8, and 70B fp16.
[01:43] Lydia Park: For acceptance criteria, our product team cares about two classes: latency and quality. Latency: p95 under 450ms for synchronous prompts at 512 tokens. Quality: on our 500 labelled prompt set, at least 88% top-1 matching of expected structured outputs. Cost: target no more than 40% uplift compared to our current internal LLM infra.
[02:05] Samir Patel: That’s helpful. A couple clarifying q's: when you say 'top-1 matching' do you mean exact string match or semantic equivalence? And is the 88% measured on raw model outputs or after any post-processing/reranking?
[02:20] Lydia Park: Good question. We mean semantic equivalence post normalization — we'll provide the normalization scripts. And validation will be run on raw model outputs before reranking.
[02:31] Clara Nguyen: Got it. We'll include two metrics in the report: normalized semantic match rate and raw token-level BLEU-ish score for structured outputs.
[02:41] Tom Briggs: For the workload trace, we can share our ELB logs — they're sampled at 1% though. Is that sufficient? We can do a short full-sample run for a 4-hour window if needed.
[02:55] Samir Patel: Prefer the uninterrupted 4-hour full sample covering your peak window — that lets us reproduce burst behavior and identify batching opportunities.
[03:04] Tom Briggs: Ok we'll get that.
[03:06] [00:03:06] Lydia Park: Also SOC2 and audit — can you confirm you've got SOC2 Type II and the relevant pen tests? Our security team will request evidence.
[03:16] Samir Patel: Yes, Redwood is SOC2 Type II. I'll attach the compliance pack. For on-prem we have an audit log integration and KMS/HSM options — though sometimes the doc shows 'Redwood Privet' instead of Private in auto-transcripts, sorry that's a known typo in our docs.
[03:31] Maya Chen: Haha, no worries. Procurement will want to see data retention and deletion guarantees, especially for PHI-adjacent PII.
[03:40] Samir Patel: Understood. For the POC we can enable zero-retention mode and provide signed Data Processing Addendum.
[03:47] Clara Nguyen: Technical note — when we run benchmarks, we will do three phases: baseline dry-run (functional), throughput runs (to capture p95), and accuracy runs (on labelled set). We'll also collect token-level cost model metrics so procurement can see unit economics.
[04:03] Eric Soto: For the reporting format, can we get a one-page executive summary with clear go/no-go flags and a detailed appendix that has raw logs and scripts?
[04:13] Samir Patel: That's our default. The one-pager will contain pass/fail for each gate and a recommended path (hosted vs dedicated vs private). The appendix will include CSVs for latency histograms, per-prompt result matrix, and cost sensitivity charts.
[04:27] Lydia Park: On the go/no-go thresholds — we want to add an availability gate: 99.5% successful requests during a 24h run, excluding scheduled maintenance and infra noise.
[04:39] Clara Nguyen: We'll define 'successful' as HTTP 200 plus non-empty model output and pass of schema validation. We'll capture schema validator errors separately.
[04:50] Tom Briggs: Another infra constraint: our network has MTU differences and we sometimes see packet fragmentation on heavy websocket streaming. Can Redwood run the streaming endpoint under those conditions? We need to avoid token truncation.
[05:03] Samir Patel: Yes, we'll add a streaming check to the runbook. For truncated streams we log partial tokens and mark as failure for the availability gate.
[05:13] [00:05:13] Clara Nguyen: Quick aside — competitors: we know you evaluated OpenAI and Anthropic; please tell us what led you to consider Redwood for this POC?
[05:25] Lydia Park: Two reasons: cost predictability and on-prem private deployment option for regulated workloads. OpenAI was great for prototyping but procurement flagged the residency and audit gaps. Anthropic's throughput on our seq length was lower in our internal tests.
[05:38] Samir Patel: Makes sense. We'll make sure the benchmark report highlights both unit cost and throughput.
[05:45] Eric Soto: We also want the spike tests — our traffic has sudden campaign-driven spikes, so we need to see autoscale performance and warmup times.
[05:56] Clara Nguyen: We'll include a spike-sim test: 10x sustained for 8 minutes and measure 95/99th latency and tail-slo breaches.
[06:07] Lydia Park: For quality acceptance, beyond the 88% semantic match, we'd like a secondary gating of 'no more than 2% hallucination rate' on our safety-labelled prompts.
[06:18] Samir Patel: Ok 'hallucination rate' — we'll rely on your labelled examples for detection and run a separate safety section in the report.
[06:26] Tom Briggs: On instrumentation: do you need agents in our infra, or can you ingest traces from S3/Cloud Storage?
[06:36] Clara Nguyen: Either is fine. For private deployment it helps to deploy our telemetry collector as a sidecar; for hosted runs we can accept logs in a signed S3 bucket. We'll document both options in the runbook.
[06:49] Maya Chen: Procurement question — if this becomes Dedicated, what's the typical contract lead time? Our legal wants to know if we can get a 60-day pilot-to-contract handoff.
[07:01] Samir Patel: Usually 30–60 days depending on entitlements and SOC attestation needs. We can draft a pilot addendum to speed things up.
[07:08] [00:07:08] Clara Nguyen: Back to metrics — proposed primary gates: latency p95 <= 450ms (sync, 512 tokens), availability >= 99.5% over 24h, semantic match >= 88% on 500 prompts, hallucination <= 2%. Secondary gates: cost delta <= 40% v internal baseline, warmup < 90s to target throughput. Are we aligned?
[07:33] Lydia Park: Yes, aligned. Also add a stability gate: no more than 1 incident of server-side 5xx per 10k requests during the run.
[07:44] Clara Nguyen: We'll add that.
[07:46] Eric Soto: How will we surface regression vs baseline? We need a single chart with delta bands.
[07:54] Samir Patel: The report will include a delta chart per metric with traffic-weighted averages and 95% CI. We'll also provide raw CSVs for your analysts.
[08:03] Tom Briggs: For the acceptance report template, one small ask: include a checklist column for 'requires infra follow-up' so we don't miss post-POC operational tasks.
[08:13] Samir Patel: Good call. We'll include that column and a runbook appendix.
[08:17] [00:08:17] Lydia Park: Can you briefly outline the timeline you propose? We want to confirm dates that line up with our risk review.
[08:24] Clara Nguyen: Proposed: week 0 — onboarding + ingest traces; week 1 — baseline + throughput runs; week 2 — accuracy and safety runs; week 3 — analysis and reporting. If we start next Monday (2025-10-27), final report ready by 2025-11-17 which is tight but feasible.
[08:43] Maya Chen: Procurement can expedite if we see the pilot addendum.
[08:47] Samir Patel: We'll draft the addendum and sample SOW.
[08:52] [00:08:52] Lily? (mislabel): sorry that's Speaker 6 glitch — question: for per-prompt variance, will you surface examples of worst-case failures?
[09:01] Clara Nguyen: Yes, top 10 worst prompts by semantic delta will be listed with raw model output, expected output, and an error taxonomy tag (schema, hallucination, timeout, truncation).
[09:14] Lydia Park: For the accuracy run, we want both micro and macro metrics — macro for fairness across prompt types.
[09:22] Samir Patel: Noted. We'll segment metrics by prompt category.
[09:26] [00:09:26] Eric Soto: Any gotchas with token accounting? Our current cost model uses tokenized units post-bpe. Will Redwood's cost numbers map directly?
[09:36] Clara Nguyen: We use token accounting aligned to commonly used BPE counts but differences can exist if you run with different vocab or custom tokenizers. We'll run the tokenizer you provide and compute unit costs on match.
[09:48] Tom Briggs: About the private deployment — will KMS integration add latency to token generation? Our compliance team is wary of callouts to key vaults every request.
[09:59] Samir Patel: We recommend caching crypto material locally in an HSM-friendly way; initial key unwrap may add a millisecond or two but shouldn't be material per token. We'll document typical latency hit for KMS integrations in the appendix.
[10:17] [00:10:17] Clara Nguyen: Ok next — reporting format specifics. We'll produce: 1) 1-page executive summary with green/amber/red gates, 2) detailed appendix with 24h latency histograms, per-prompt matrix (CSV), cost sensitivity tables, and raw logs, 3) runbook with steps to reproduce and infra checklist. Anything else?
[10:32] Lydia Park: Include a short 'assumptions' section that lists environment differences (tokenizer, pre/post processing, network variance).
[10:41] Samir Patel: Will do.
[10:43] Maya Chen: For sign-off, who from BlueWave should sign the acceptance? We need an internal approval flow.
[10:50] Lydia Park: I'll be the primary sign-off on ML metrics, Tom will sign-off on infra, and Maya will sign for procurement. We'll circulate the signed PDF.
[10:59] Samir Patel: Excellent. We'll make the acceptance section a table with name, role, and digital signature placeholder.
[11:06] [00:11:06] Clara Nguyen: Last technical note — we'll also include a lightweight reproducibility bundle: dockerfile, run scripts, and a small subset of prompts and expected outputs so you can run locally if needed.
[11:18] Lydia Park: That will help security scoping.
[11:22] Eric Soto: Anything else on risk triggers — for example if hallucination spikes during spike tests, do we auto-fail?
[11:31] Clara Nguyen: We'll mark that as a hard fail for quality gate. The report will include a 'severity' field — hard fail vs tolerance breach.
[11:40] Tom Briggs: One more infra note — instrument the 95/99 percentiles with request IDs so we can trace requests end-to-end.
[11:48] Samir Patel: We'll ensure request-id propagation is part of the telemetry collector.
[11:52] [00:11:52] Lydia Park: Great. To recap briefly, agreed gates: latency p95 <=450ms, availability >=99.5%, semantic match >=88%, hallucination <=2%, cost uplift <=40% — plus stability/no excessive 5xx. Deliverables: benchmark runbook, one-pager, appendix, reproducibility bundle. Action owners noted.
[12:16] Samir Patel: Thanks — Samir will share the runbook and draft template by Thursday 2025-10-23, Clara will run cost sims by 10/27, BlueWave will provide workload traces by 10/24. We'll plan a sync on 2025-10-29 for network checklist.
[12:31] Maya Chen: Thanks all.
[12:33] Eric Soto: Thanks.
[12:34] [00:12:34] Meeting ends.

Notes on transcription: speakers mislabelled around 11:06 as 'Lily?' which is actually Speaker 6, occasional mistranscriptions: 'Redwood Privet' -> Redwood Private; 'KV cache' sometimes appears as 'K V cash'. We left those verbatim in places.

References/links shared in chat (to be attached post-call): benchmark-spreadsheet-link (placeholder), compliance-pack.pdf (samir/redwood link), runbook-draft.md (to be uploaded).

End of transcript.
